messages.subject: Day sleep detection
parts:
Hi everyone,
First of all, thanks Vincent and others collaborators for all your work. I'm new at actigraphy field and I started to try some packages to use in my phD. Finally, I choose GGIR and I hope to learn and do future help in this work.

With this in mind, I ran a batch of raw GeneActiv files with this comand:

g.shell.GGIR(
     datadir="/Volumes/actigraphy/data/1479", 
     outputdir="/Volumes/actigraphy", 
     mode = c(1,2,3,4,5), 
     do.visual=TRUE, 
     viewingwindow = 1, 
     visualreport = TRUE, 
     epochvalues2csv = TRUE
     )

After, I took a look to the results, I got almost no detection (only 1 in 14) in day sleep. Is it normal? I attached the report. My GGIR version is 2.2 and R version is 3.6.2.

Thanks in Advance,
Francisco.


P.S.: I don't know if this information is relevant, but, In this folder (1479) of my example, I have 8 .bin files from the same person. In this file I have 30 consecutive days of use in 20Hz.

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Day sleep detection
parts:
Hi Francisco,

Great to hear you were able to figure out how to run GGIR.

Are you referring to part 4 csv reports when you refer to "After, I took a look to the results, I got almost no detection (only 1 in 14) in day sleep"? Please note that the .pdf visualisation you attached is not supposed to show daytime 'sleep'.

GGIR produces estimates of daytime 'sustained inactivity bouts', which is a term I introduced to avoid having to call them naps. Calling it daytime sleep or daytime napping is tricky as there are no studies that have directly investigated the validity of this. I do not think the PSG night-time studies I did are sufficient to support the claim that nap detection is reliable. Further, short lasting non-wear periods (< 15 minutes) that are missed by the non-wear detection are likely to be labelled as sustained inactivity bout. So, I think it is best to interpret them or their absence carefully.

Whether it is plausible to not see sustained inactivity bout in your participants also depends on whether you expect them to take naps or to take off the sensor for short periods of time.

Cheers,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant
https://accelting.com/
